notes.title: Community Update #2
notes.notes:
[p]After two long months without any tasty news to share, somewhat depriving you of clarity about progress on things we've been struggling with, we're finally coming up for some air…[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/8e55c0cc3fddb168ec4f685e9cbcd018f17693fd.png"][/img][img src="data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAPABAP///wAAACH5BAEKAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAICRAEAOw=="][/img]​[/p][p]You know that moment when you want to tidy up a room… and you end up emptying everything onto the floor before you even get started? That's more or less what we did with WAVEN. The clock was ticking, and behind the scenes, we simplified, redesigned, trimmed, reimagined, and sometimes even daydreamed… Between two heated meetings and a number of admittedly heavy game design documents, we pulled ourselves together, keeping one clear idea in mind: How can we make WAVEN simpler without taking anything away from it? As much as we love complex systems, lengthy combos, and mind-blowing builds, there comes a time where even we lose sight of what we're actually doing. So we decided to pick our battles a bit better.[/p][p][/p][h2][u]SIMPLIFICATION[/u][/h2][p]As surprising as it may seem, simplifying a game isn't simple. Quite the opposite – it's a really convoluted task. The word "simplification" can be intimidating because it brings to mind losing depth, mechanics becoming bland, and fun being restricted. But that's absolutely not the goal. What we're aiming for is clarity. A game that makes you want to dive in head first, without wondering if you'll be out of your depth. Rereading a spell description six (or more) times to grasp what it does? We don't go in for that anymore. So, we gathered our courage and tackled several fundamental aspects of WAVEN:[/p][list][*][p][b]heroes[/b] and their [b]spells,[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]descriptions,[/b][/p][/*][*][p]the [b]card system,[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]companions,[/b][/p][/*][*][p]the [b]AP reserve,[/b][/p][/*][*][p]and a few [b]removed mechanics…[/b][/p][/*][/list][p]
[/p][h3]Heroes and Their Spells[/h3][p]Those who followed our Ankama Live in April already got a glimpse of it… but let's lay things out plainly. In the new version of WAVEN, each hero has four unique spells and a passive that is unique to them. That's all there is to the character's identity. All other spells (some 150) are now shared by all heroes – no more class spells, no more impossible builds because "Dang, I want to play that, but it's not for this class". As for hero passives, we're planning to rework all of them, but we'll come back to this in a future post about this project.[/p][p][/p][h3]Descriptions[/h3][p]Many of you pointed this out to us, sometimes kindly, sometimes less so – spell descriptions were often mysterious. Too long, too technical, too obscure. And we've got to admit, you were right. So we went over it all again, word by word, line by line. The goal? For each spell to clearly state what it does, when, and how, without requiring you to get out a cross-reference table in Excel. We shortened text length, standardized terms, and reworked the order of information. The result? Spells that can be understood by reading them once, without any confusing jargon. And when the effect is a bit more unique, we make it more understandable, either visually or contextually.[/p][p][/p][h3]The Card System[/h3][p]As we already mentioned, your cards are at the heart of WAVEN's gameplay. Spells and companions are now grouped together in the deck. And that changes everything. Each deck now consists of 16 cards, which you can choose freely from among your spells and companions. Spells still cost Action Points, while companions require Command Points. To earn CP, you have to perform specific actions on the board or play specific spell cards. In combat, you will now have up to nine cards in your hand (instead of seven previously), giving you greater flexibility, more tactical choices, and most of all, less frustration with draws (and less repetitiveness in combat). We wanted each turn to make players think, but also react. Behind this overhaul is a clear intention to reunify systems, avoid overlapping layers that don't go well together, and focus the player's attention on one thing – how they play and why. And since all (or almost all) cards are now shared between heroes, the game also becomes more generous in how it lets you build a deck.[/p][p][/p][h3]Companions[/h3][p]Companions… What a wonderful topic. They weren't really spells, not really heroes, often useful… and sometimes killed during the first round. Basically, it was time to put them back at the center of gameplay.[/p][p][/p][p]Companions are now cards in their own right, on a par with spells. They follow the same deckbuilding rules, are played from your hand, and finally have a real strategic space where they can exist. You no longer place them "because you have to" or to achieve a passive effect – you choose them, you play them, and you evolve them. This last point is important because you can now evolve a companion that is already on the field. Since they exist in the form of cards, once played, they return to your draw pile (like a spell). If you draw them again while they are still on the field, you can make them rank up by replaying their card directly on them at a reduced CP cost. Each evolution improves their attack and health stats and heals them.[/p][p][/p][p]Outside of combat, companions can still level up like any other item in the deck. This costs copies of the relevant hero… and a few kamas. When they reach a given level, each companion unlocks a unique special spell that is specific to their own story. This spell is automatically added to your hand when the companion is summoned or when they perform a dedicated action on the field. These special spells all have a narrative link to the relevant hero and make it possible to replay certain original, iconic, or simply fun-to-play actions.[/p][p][/p][p]The most observant among you will most likely recognize the artist behind the companion cards' new visual design… We've prepared an interview that will be released sometime later.[/p][p][/p][p]We've also made a decision that might just delight some of you. We've expanded the pool of companions with other legends from the Krosmoz and removed those who weren't historical figures (especially characters from the game [i]KROSMAGA[/i]). You'll find these changes directly in the game.[/p][p][/p][h3]The AP Reserve[/h3][p]It doesn't exist anymore… or at least, not in the same form. During our playtesting, we realized that the AP reserve was an unnatural mechanic for new players. In other words, they didn't understand it, so they didn't play it.[/p][p][/p][p]So, we've adjusted how it works. Some spells still let you generate additional AP, but instead of storing them so you can activate them when you want, these AP will now be automatically added to your total on the following turn.[/p][p][/p][h3]Removed Mechanics[/h3][p]This section might set your teeth on edge. We get it. But it's necessary in order for you to understand where we want to go with WAVEN. Nothing is set in stone – [b]the choices we're presenting here are where we are now, so they might still change before the game is officially launched.[/b][/p][p][/p][p][b]We've decided to remove the skill profile and all items from the game (rings, armbands, and brooches).[/b][/p][p][/p][p]Why? Because as we kept adding layers, the game became incomprehensible. Worse still, the systems interfered with each other, requiring lengthy testing sessions after equally lengthy theory-crafting sessions, just to validate the desired combos.[/p][p][/p][p]The skill profile particularly didn't encourage diversity in builds. For most heroes, a single path naturally stood out as "the best", which ended up restricting the fun.[/p][p][/p][p]The same was true of items, which mainly added density without any real depth. Too many micro-effects, too many special cases ("I've got to equip this ring before the other one so that its bonuses will be fully activated…"), and clearly not enough instant fun.[/p][p][/p][p]So, we decided to make a more comprehensible and structured game, starting over with a clean foundation and reinventing things. New forms of build customization could emerge later on.[/p][h2][u]THE HOME SCREEN[/u][/h2][p]You've seen it time and again, liked it, and even complimented it. The home screen was mainly used to select your server, click the "PLAY" button, and admire the fantastic work of Sad! and Franho on the seasonal visual design. It was nice, and it set the mood, but that was about it.[/p][p][b]We thought, "What if…"[/b][/p][p]What if this screen became the game's main hub, a gateway to all available modes? What would it look like? Would the available content be clearer? Would navigating between the different game experiences be easier?[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/6c52be9858845f2a472402b3450e91913868b07e.png"][/img][img src="data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAPABAP///wAAACH5BAEKAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAICRAEAOw=="][/img]​[/p][p][i](Image not representative of the final result)[/i][/p][p][/p][p]So this is where it all begins. Each game mode is illustrated by its own card, key information (progress and rank), a short explanatory tooltip, and "let's go". It's a good way for us to highlight new features and seasonal events. It's also a good way for you to select the mode you like best at any time.[/p][p][b]The stated mode names are not final.[/b][/p][p]You already know [b]Story Mode[/b] – it's WAVEN's PvE mode. You no longer have to start an adventure (create a character) in this mode to unlock PvP and competitive modes.[/p][p][/p][p]We told you about [b]Special Stories[/b] in the 2023 KrosmoNote under the name of "Heroic Quests". The idea is to offer immersive transmedia narrative content where you will relive major events from the Krosmoz. For example, fighting the Taurs during their invasion of the Puddly Village in the Wakfu Era ([i]WAKFU[/i] – Season 1, Episode 5: [i]The Magnificent Five[/i]), or the epic battle pitting Oropo and his allies against Grougaloragran and his brother Chibi on Oma Island ([i]Oropo – Battle for the Eliacube[/i]).[/p][p][/p][p][b]Roguelike [/b](or "Survival") is our favorite playground right now (the first one being [b]Expeditions[/b]). This mode has developed quite a bit since we talked about it in the last WAVEN Ankama Live, so we'll come back to it in a future post, because it clearly deserves its own section.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Boss Fight [/b](sometimes called "Battle Royale") will be the next system we tackle once [b]Roguelike[/b] has been finalized. We can already tell you that all the work done on [b]Roguelike[/b] will speed up production for [b]Boss Fight,[/b] since both modes share a number of mechanics.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/03abc750d84010d57ca85039907c1f36fbd6e8d5.png"][/img][img src="data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAPABAP///wAAACH5BAEKAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAICRAEAOw=="][/img]​[/p][p][i](Image not representative of the final result)[/i][/p][p][/p][p]You also know [b]Versus.[/b] And no, we haven't done any more work on it yet.
[b]Season[/b] mode is the good old seasonal fight in the Time Portal. It hasn't been worked on yet either, not for the time being.[/p][p][/p][p]Finally, the modes on the far right of the screen are merely placeholders that are there to help you (and us) visualize what this home screen will look like when new content appears.[/p][p][/p][p]So as you can see, [b]there's still plenty to do and share with you.[/b] We can't wait for you to try out this new version of WAVEN and be honest with us: Is it better? Does it work? Does it make you want to come back? In any case, we really think it does.[/p][p][b]Thank you for your patience and messages. But more importantly, thank you for still being here. More is yet to come.[/b][/p]

notes.title: FAQ – Progress Reset
notes.notes:
A new era is about to dawn for WAVEN and with it, there will be a major progress reset. Before that happens, we're explaining everything simply and openly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/78179552c75e3df93ed0e0cb7fe4de913027ea4b.png[/img]

[h2][u]WHY A RESET?[/u][/h2]
With the arrival of major changes in the game, this reset is needed to ensure a healthier and more balanced experience that is better prepared to welcome the upcoming new content and features. WAVEN's overall balance is going to undergo a structural change, and it is therefore [b]crucial[/b] that accounts be wiped clean.

 

[b]Don't worry! Everything you've acquired that has lasting value will be kept or refunded.[/b]

 
[h2][u]WHAT WILL BE RESET[/u][/h2]
The reset concerns, above all, everything related to your [b]in-game progress:[/b]
[list]	[*]World [b]chapters,[/b] [b]quest points,[/b] [b]first-time rewards,[/b] and progress in [b]Story Mode[/b][/*]	[*][b]Characters[/b][/*]	[*][b]Items:[/b] spells, companions, equipment, chests, etc.[/*]	[*][b]Soft currency:[/b] kamas, island tokens, Wakfu fragments, season tickets, runes, etc.[/*]	[*][b]Guilds[/b][/*]	[*][b]Cosmetic items earned[/b] through account progress[/*]	[*][b]Boats[/b][/*]	[*][b]Prisms[/b][/*][/list]
 
[h2][u]WHAT WILL BE KEPT[/u][/h2]
Some elements [b]will be maintained,[/b] because they are linked to purchases or exceptional events:
[list]	[*]Cosmetic items [b]purchased with gems[/b] (or refunded if they are not compatible with the new version of the game, such as guild haven skins, etc.)[/*]	[*]Cosmetic items [b]won through community events:[/b] trophies, character customizations, etc.[/*]	[*][b]Gameplay comfort elements:[/b] character slots, deck slots, etc. (or refunded if they cannot be kept)[/*]	[*]Your [b]gems,[/b] both bought and earned[/*][/list]
 
[h2][u]WHAT WILL BE REFUNDED AUTOMATICALLY[/u][/h2]
We will refund everything that couldn't be kept and pertains to purchases or removed features:
[list]	[*][b]Guild haven skins[/b][/*]	[*][b]Shop packs containing gameplay elements[/b][/*][/list] [h2][b]The automatic refund is separate from future compensations, which will be communicated later.[/b][/h2]
 

 
[h2][u]USEFUL INFO[/u][/h2]
Most of the elements that will be [b]kept or refunded[/b] will be sent via an [b]in-game message.[/b] You'll need to [b]open the message and recover its contents[/b] to activate the elements in your account.

 

[u]A few important things:[/u]
[list]	[*]The contents of this message [b]are not transferable[/b] to another account or another server.[/*]	[*]This message [b]will not have an expiration date.[/b][/*]	[*]However, we reserve the right to [b]force automatic recovery[/b] of its content on your account.[/*][/list]
 
[h2][u]WHEN WILL THE RESET HAPPEN?[/u][/h2]
This complete reset will happen when [b]version 1.0 of WAVEN launches.[/b] It will be [b]automatic and transparent.[/b] No prior action will be required of you. You will, however, need to recover the kept elements from you in-game message.

 
[h2][u]ANY QUESTIONS?[/u][/h2]
We've tried to be as exhaustive and transparent as possible, but you may still have questions. Post your questions in the comments below this FAQ. We'll answer them as they are posted and complete this article so that everyone can find the answers to their questions.

notes.title: AnkamaLive: WAVEN in 2025 (recap)
notes.notes:
Did you miss the latest Ankama Live on WAVEN's future? This article summarizes the big announcements and major changes to come in the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/700813ddbdc2c7a0f35f67d9184e520584f4624e.png[/img]

[b]The game has not been abandoned in the slightest.[/b]

 

WAVEN is an adventure that we dreamed of, designed, and built with passion. A license in which we deeply believe. We love it. It is a game that we want to be a worthy heir of everything that DOFUS and WAKFU are and have been for millions of players. We've carried this project for a long time and we still believe in it with conviction, even though recently the wind has been blowing much less in its sails…

 

When the early access launched, the momentum was thunderous. The game found its audience, which was curious and enthusiastic. More than one million players came aboard, at least once, in this devastated World of Twelve. That's huge. Today, however, approximately seven thousand players log on daily. And, let's be honest, that's not a sign of good health.

 

Not enough content, not enough diversity in gameplay modes, a vague promise about its positioning, hesitant management – examples are not lacking. We know, we see it, we're experiencing it with you. We need to stop the bleeding and stop patching leaks. We've taken a step back, dug deeper, examined the very essence of WAVEN and its structure and ambitions. Because if we want it to continue to exist, we need to give it a second wind. During this process, we fundamentally challenged our beliefs, following a clear objective: [b]rebuild on solid foundations.[/b]

 
[h2][u]CURRENT SITUATION[/u][/h2]
Before talking about rebuilding, we needed a true diagnosis. Not some polished or embellished report. Instead, something clear, precise, sometimes difficult to hear, and yet [b]necessary.[/b] Because to understand where WAVEN stumbled, we first needed to be willing to [b]look reality in the face,[/b] head on without filters. The game is suffering from several clearly identified flaws. Some are structural, other more subtle, and all contribute to the impression of an imbalance, an unfulfilled promise.

 

In this section, we're going to discuss the main points that pushed us to hit the "stop" button. Not to abandon ship, but to get it seaworthy again with a clearer, more coherent, healthier direction. Because we don't want to just "hang on" – [b]we want to do better.[/b]

[h3]Overly Complex Game Rules[/h3]
WAVEN isn't an easy game to master. That's not necessarily a problem in and of itself. Breadth and depth are qualities we are proud of, but they need to be in the right proportions, and both understandable and accessible.[b] [/b]Today, the game's learning curve is too steep. Between the mechanics specific to each class, the contextual spell effects, companions, runes, elements, and passive mechanics that are barely explained… players can easily feel lost. Too many systems piled on systems, unnatural connections, the main elements not showcased enough. And, a learning curve that, instead of motivating players, ends up discouraging them. We had planned a game for PC and mobile, with a mobile-first approach. We therefore need to improve this approach.

 
[h3]Good Acquisition, Poor Retention[/h3]
The results are undeniable – we know how to attract people. The look, the universe, the ties with the Krosmoz, the cross-platform strategy… WAVEN intrigues, seduces, makes you want to try it. But desire fades. Many players only stay a few days, and quickly do the rounds of what we have to offer. Some don't click with the gameplay, while others don't have enough of a reason to come back. It's missing a spine – an encouraging game loop, the feeling of tangible progress, and clear landmarks. Today, the game gives too little, too late, or not in the right way.

 
[h3]Monetization Problems[/h3]
WAVEN doesn't bring in enough. There's no reason to beat around the bush. The game's current economic model is not viable. The offer is too light, based only on customization, and doesn't work as we would have liked. We need to find other levers to make the project sustainable.

 
[h3]Overly Elitist Competitive Modes[/h3]
The current PvP system is demanding, sometimes too much so. Gaps in preparation, frustrations due to balancing, and the lack of balanced matchmaking irritate attractiveness. This results in a confidential competitive scene, which is not very welcoming, and doesn't allow for the creation of a lasting community dynamic. Entry is complex because you have to manage a new, specialized deck for PvP that, in addition, has no relation to the PvE deck. We want to head toward competition that is more fun and more accessible.

 
[h3]Lack of Clear Objectives[/h3]
People start playing WAVEN… but why stay? The game doesn't provide enough guidance. The short-, medium- and long-term objectives are cruelly lacking in visibility, or don't even exist. There isn't a sense of strong progress or an end goal. This vagueness impacts players' motivation. Without a destination, it's difficult to find one's way, invest, project and get attached. Even the most curious players eventually start turning in circles, because concrete perspectives are missing.

 

[b]Let's offer something better.[/b]
[h2][u]SIMPLIFY GAME RULES[/u][/h2]
Work overhauling deckbuilding is already well underway. We are going to deepen the card system while reworking the interface and ergonomics, in both the deck editor and combat. The goal? Make theory crafting and combat more fluid and intuitive. This starts, first and foremost, with the relationship between companions and spells. Currently, summoning a companion depends on the elemental gauges, which are themselves fed by spells. This cascading mechanism makes the experience unnecessarily complex, while also reducing the possibility of combos. We'll be breaking this link.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/db50d749705689158145502ae4fba346a4daa659.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/d6e9824cc6bafd0c815230cd76a994f9a8573523.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/7e94de35ac62e9945c6ebef224accdbf52e23b59.png[/img]
[i]Illustrations not representative of the final contents in-game.[/i]

 

Henceforth, [b]the deck will be composed of 16 cards[/b] distributed freely among spells and companions. Summoning a companion will require you to accumulate [b]Command Points,[/b] generated by spells. There won't be an elemental link between the two. A spell of any element will be able to provide Command Points, letting you summon any companion.

 

The spell and companion progression system will stay similar to the current system. This is, you'll need to collect several copies of the same card to upgrade it.

 

When it comes to equipment, we're moving to what's essential: four (4) items per hero maximum: a ring, an armband, a consumable (item with charges offering experience or loot bonuses or summoning a special enemy in combat) and an emblem (discussed later in this article).
[h3]Deckbuilding Overhaul[/h3]
To have a clear understanding of our vision of simplification, we also need to discuss classes and items. Currently, each class has too many spells, which makes balancing both complex and laborious. We are going to [b]recenter mechanics:[/b] a [b]base of common spells[/b] will be able to be used by all heroes, from all classes. This change will let us avoid redundancy, notably for status effects. Each hero will, of course, keep a few [b]exclusive spells[/b] ensuring their identity. Finally, we want to do away with cascading tooltips. In other words: allow players to understand the effect of a spell or item with a glance. The information must be direct, readable, and immediately understandable.

 

[b]We don't want a punitive simplification, but rather a clearer, more fun simplification.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/e84c28bfe1a36a96a0f5aa127a73f1ba270cb3c4.png[/img]
[i]Illustration not representative of the final contents in-game.[/i]

Several elements should be noted:
[list]	[*]Gauges and companion slots have been removed from the left side of the screen.[/*]	[*]Reserve Action Points have been removed.[/*]	[*]Companion and spell cards are in the same hand.[/*]	[*]The hand has nine cards in total, compared to the current seven.[/*]	[*]Command Points are located next to Action Points.[/*]	[*]The combat log hasn't been removed – it is being overhauled.[/*]	[*]A new gauge, represented by the class symbol, is located next to the AP and CP - the "Special" gauge.[/*][/list][h3]What's a "Special"?[/h3]
The Special is a new mechanic added to the gameplay of each hero. Each hero will have their own special blows – unique capabilities, strong actions that reflect their personality and gameplay style. To trigger a special blow, the hero will have to equip an Emblem and fill a special gauge in combat, then play their blow when the time seems right. This gauge fills with actions: when the hero attacks, when a companion does damage, or even via certain spells.

 

For example, one of Bovalor Orok's special blows makes the hero charge at all in-line characters. Pikuxala Hand causes the hero to teleport to a cell adjacent to all enemies, triggering the hero's power on each teleportation.

 

Emblems, for their part, are new items that unlock around level 45 to 50.

 

[b]The game is simpler, clearer, and easier to understand.[/b]

 
[h2][u]IMPROVE RETENTION[/u][/h2]
Introducing players to WAVEN is one thing. The real challenge, though, is getting them to want to stay. To rise to this challenge, we've rethought the heart of the gaming experience: the game loop, progression, and above all… the fun.
[h3]Clearer Objectives[/h3]
This subject deserves its own section. We'll discuss it later on in this article.

 
[h3]Level 100 to Reach[/h3]
Back to the beginning… The maximum level for characters will increase from 50 to [b]100,[/b] with more fluid, more rewarding, and better distributed leveling up. This change will make it possible to offer more engaging progression over the long term and to ensure that players' levels better match the enemies they face by avoiding absurd gaps (such as a level-50 player fighting level-120 monsters) that hinder comprehension.

 
[h3]Cards to Collect and Upgrade[/h3]
As mentioned above, the deckbuilding will now rely on a [b]new card system.[/b] Each card can evolve, be upgraded, and offer new gameplay possibilities. A system designed to encourage collection and the fun of optimization.

 
[h3]New Game Modes[/h3]
We're planning for the arrival of [b]new modes,[/b] both competitive and not, all of which focused on one promise: [i]fun![/i] They will enrich the overall experience, so that each game session is different, lively and a source of enjoyment.

 
[h3]Collect Crew… Monsters![/h3]
This is another point we'll expand on below. Just know that players will be able to get a new type of loot in dungeons: [b]crew monsters.[/b] These creatures will fuel an entirely new game mode.

 
[h3]Items with Variable Stats[/h3]
This is something new in WAVEN. Henceforth, [b]items will have variable stats.[/b] No more fixed equipment: every piece of loot will count and every item will be able to be optimized.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/8aa9e990a19afd20e817239ed400b8b4881da997.png[/img]
[i]Illustration not representative of the final contents in-game.[/i]

 

[b]We want to bring what's most valuable back to loot: thrills.[/b]

 

For that, we're introducing a [b]new equipment evolution logic,[/b] closer to what we already offer in DOFUS and WAKFU. A system structured into level bands, with items that have [b]variable stats[/b] and [b]true rise in power:[/b]
[list]	[*]Items will be distributed in [b]level bands[/b] (1–10, 11–20, etc.) and can be equipped if your character has reached the required level.[/*]	[*][b]Only one[/b] variable stat per item.[/*]	[*]If you get an [b]identical item with a better stat,[/b] the first one will automatically be [b]recycled[/b] as a resource.[/*]	[*]If the new stat is [b]not as good,[/b] the new one will be recycled.[/*]	[*]If you item is [b]already at max level,[/b] each new copy will let you [b]increase some of its masteries.[/b][/*]	[*]Armbands will offer masteries of the ATTACK archetype while rings will be for MAGIC.[/*][/list]
 
[h2][u]OVERHAUL MONETIZATION[/u][/h2]
The monetization in WAVEN doesn't work. We had bet on a model focused on cosmetic items, convinced that that would be enough to sustain the game. We were wrong. The numbers speak for themselves: the game doesn't generate enough income to be viable over the long term.

Monetization is a sensitive subject, as we're well aware. We are determined: [b]no subscriptions[/b] like in DOFUS, [b]no pay-to-win,[/b] but instead an honest, reasonable [b]pay-to-fast[/b] approach. That is to say that we want to allow players to [b]save time,[/b] not gain advantages in combat.

 

The Battle Pass system will stay in place but will be tweaked. It will continue to offer [b]cosmetic rewards,[/b] with progress based on [b]daily, weekly[/b] and [b]season missions,[/b] a bit like now.

 

We're also working on the adding "comfort services" inspired by what we have already in [b]DOFUS Touch[/b] and [b]WAKFU.[/b] These options will let players simplify or smooth their in-game experience [b]without influencing their power or combat mechanics.[/b]

 

This new approach to monetization is still a work in progress. Why? Because it's essential that we [b]lay solid foundations first[/b] for gameplay, progression and content before building a coherent offer that [b]respects[/b] our players. Nevertheless, you now know [b]our guiding principles:[/b] more clarity, more diversity, [b]without ever compromising fairness.[/b]

 
[h2][u]COMPETITIVE MODES: MORE ACCESSIBLE, FAIRER[/u][/h2]
The current competitive system does not live up to our ambitions. Today, the best players crush newcomers, and a PvP mode accessible from the start is not a guarantee of fairness, but a source of frustration. Going forward, in "competitive" modes, [b]decks will be prebuilt.[/b]
[h3]Prebuilt Decks[/h3]
Prebuilt decks will be drawn from a multitude of decks, designed by the [i]game design[/i] team and, for every match, players will have a limited, random selection of decks to choose from. These decks will evolve, notably thanks to you and your feedback. This new system will let us [b]quickly adjust[/b] power imbalances between decks, [b]avoid dominating compositions[/b] and guarantee a healthier and more dynamic playing field for everyone.

 
[h3]1VS1 & 2VS2 PVP Mode[/h3]
We are going to rework the interface, ergonomics and rankings, and offer matchmaking.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/7fcc25532ea8aae1952f71e15a6294d536a75b75.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/aa627919a5942b2f2ef6600d2d5258493b569e44.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/37ceda38542bf30f03809d6b493ab0b1668bdcbc.png[/img]
[i]Illustrations not representative of the final contents in-game.[/i]

 
[h3](COOPERATIVE OR COMPETITIVE) "Survival" Mode[/h3]
Formerly known by the name of "Boss Fight", this mode will be coming back in a new format that we need to rename because there isn't necessarily one big bad boss in the center of the board.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/00d9fde47ebf55075d9eaae1155d867bad0cfe08.png[/img]
[i]Illustration not representative of the final contents in-game.[/i]

Two variants will be offered:
[list]	[*][b]Competitive:[/b] Four (4) players will face off. Each player will face the same waves but can use specific actions to hinder their opponents. In this mode, all the players play at the same time, then it's the enemy's turn. And so on… until only one survivor is left.[/*]	[*][b]Cooperative:[/b] Four (4) players will band together to survive as long as possible against a shared enemy. This variant will be found on the Monster Islands, and turns will happen like in dungeons.[/*][/list]
 

With every monster they eliminate, the player will earn points, shown in a specific interface (located to the right of the combat screen). These points can be used to buy [b]companions[/b] or [b]spells[/b] that are [b]exclusive[/b] to the current fight. The contents of the shop will [b]evolve as waves go by,[/b] and there will be the option to [b]manually refresh[/b] the things on offer.

 
[h3](COOPETITIVE) "Wave Fight" Mode[/h3]
Previously called "roguelike", this mode is coming back with a twist – more ambitious, but always faithful to its essence: [b]fight wave after wave of monsters,[/b] push back limits and go even further.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/531addb821b6c2e81f6bad3b6859de96f4958b6f.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/62c64bca31b3ed39c0bbe9f08bd316129c2f1b2b.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/688f529911948418e274455e7b3f4c9676d2eeaf.png[/img]
[i]Illustrations not representative of the final contents in-game.[/i]

Here, [b]cooperation is crucial.[/b] Two players will form a duo and join forces to progress through a huge number of waves, with the goal of going as far as possible or perhaps even defeating the final waves. The final score will determine their place in a [b]specific leaderboard.[/b]

 

The shop system will still be present, like the one in Survival mode, and players will be able to spend the points they earn to buy [b]spells or companions exclusive to the fight,[/b] with options that will evolve as they progress.

 

Fights are [b]classic turn-based,[/b] like in dungeons. But this time, the arena's scaling up: [b]larger boards,[/b] some with [b]new shapes,[/b] like we saw in the fights against Toross Mordal and Cire Momore.

 
[h3](ASYNCHRONOUS) Expeditions[/h3]
One of WAVEN's initial promises was to offer an asynchronous mode. We had already tested a system in conjunction with the Haven Islands and their defense, but the formula didn't win us over. Today, we believe in another approach that will be more fun: sending a crew across the high seas, fighting other players, and collecting loot.

 

[b]Note that in this mode, fights will play out automatically.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/f0b3cfcb79895b3b546ada52d1d90422f4d4a2c5.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/9cd1bfe669850d938504ab0630f9009a635445fd.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/bfd2f1cbc4e5a28fba07af24fe7204c1e0f11065.png[/img]
[i]Illustrations not representative of the final contents in-game.[/i]

 

The principle is simple: form a team consisting of [b]a captain[/b] and [b]four sailors,[/b] choose their [b]ship,[/b] and send them out adventuring on the (not so calm) seas of WAVEN.

 

The crew members are a [b]new type of loot[/b] that can be found on the Monster Islands:
[list]	[*]The [b]captains[/b] can be collected in the dungeon [b]detours.[/b][/*]	[*]The [b]sailors[/b] may drop during [b]any fight[/b] on the island in question.[/*]	[*]The [b]ships,[/b] for their part, will need to be [b]built[/b] using new, specific [b]resources.[/b][/*][/list] 
Each ship will give [b]variable bonuses:[/b] the more imposing it is, the more significant the effects will be.
 

The crew monsters will have [b]their regular characteristics and powers,[/b] as in PvE fights. This opens a path to [b]brand new combinations.[/b]

 

Like spells and companions, crew members will be able to [b]level up[/b] by getting more copies of their cards. An [b]additional resource[/b] will be needed to finalize their rise in power.

 

Once the crew is ready, the player will launch the expedition. A [b]countdown[/b] will start, showing how much time is needed before the ship comes back. When it comes back, the player will get:
[list]	[*]the [b]rewards[/b] collected along the way, and[/*]	[*]an [b]expedition log,[/b] detailing the maritime events that happened during the crossing.[/*][/list]
 

Before setting sail, each member of the crew will need to be [b]placed with care[/b] on the board. Three full rows will be available, offering [b]freedom for strategic placement.[/b] The player will be able to test several compositions to find the best configuration.

 

Once the expedition is over, [b]each fight will be available to be watched in a playback,[/b] so players can analyze their choices, assess efficiency, and [b]adapt their strategies[/b] for the seagoing expedition.

 
[h2][u]THE GOAL OF THE GAME[/u][/h2]
We want to offer a clear direction, a true shared quest, a reason to go on an adventure in WAVEN. This is a crucial element that is currently missing today. Like DOFUS with the hunt for the six Dofus, and like WAKFU with the fight against Ogrest, [b]WAVEN must also offer a strong end goal,[/b] an [b]adversary,[/b] a [b]threat,[/b] and a [b]central objective[/b] to achieve, the identity of which will be revealed a little later.

 

Simultaneously, we also want to [b]give the Haven Islands back their value.[/b] Today, [b]they are cruelly lacking in concrete interest,[/b] except for the most faithful collectors. We haven't yet found the right formula: [b]a system that is relevant, attractive and reasonable in terms of development resources[/b] all at the same time. The evolution of Haven Islands will therefore come [b]later,[/b] but it is a goal we care deeply about.

 
[h2][u]THE ROADMAP THROUGH THE END OF THE YEAR[/u][/h2]
Our promises only bind those who believe in them. And we, well, we believe in them. We believe in ourselves and in our ability to stay on course and do better. Above all, we believe in you – this community that has stuck with WAVEN in high winds, rough seas, and reconstruction. Today, the team's work is underway. Many areas of work are progressing in parallel, each in its own specialty, with a shared objective: finally offer a [b]complete formula[/b] that is [b]clear[/b] and [b]solid[/b] for WAVEN.

 

We also want to keep you better informed, more regularly, via devblog articles, shared visuals, livestreams, etc. It's time to show what is happening behind the scenes.

 

Given the magnitude of the changes to come, we are [b]pausing the Battle Pass system.[/b] Continuing to produce season fights and new cosmetic items doesn't make sense when the game experience is going to be profoundly transformed. That's right: there [b]won't be any content updates[/b] in the foreseeable future.
That said, the team will continue to maintain the servers and [b]bugfixes[/b] may be deployed as needed.

 

[b]Two major stages in our crosshairs.[/b]

 

Between now and the end of the year, we are aiming for two crucial stages for WAVEN:
[list]	[*][b]An initial test version[/b] of the new systems, ideally in [b]September.[/b]
	If certain elements are ready sooner, we'll open an [b]early test build.[/b][/*]	[*][b]The global release of version 1.0,[/b] hopefully in [b]December.[/b]
	That will, of course, depend on the test phases going well and if we stick to our schedule. If needed, we won't hesitate to [b]take more time[/b] even if that means [b]carrying over into 2026.[/b][/*][/list]
 
[h2][u]PROGRESS RESET: A DIFFICULT BUT NECESSARY DECISION[/u][/h2]
With an overhaul of this scope of the game, its fundamental mechanics, its evolution systems, its goals and its game modes, it is [b]impossible to maintain the current progress as such.[/b] This is a decision we did not take lightly or without measuring the consequences.

 

[b]Players' progress will be reset.[/b]

Levels, spells, companions, items, resources, characters… all progress systems will be reset to zero to start off again on a coherent and balanced base that is above all suited to the new version of WAVEN.

 

This decision is necessary for several reasons:
[list]	[*][b]Because the rules are changing.[/b] Spells, companions, items and deckbuilding: everything has been rethought. Keeping the former system would be a source of inconsistencies and unfairness.[/*]	[*][b]Because the game economy is changing.[/b] Resources, loot, item rarity, and progress value won't mean the same thing.[/*]	[*][b]Because we don't want to force the old world to live alongside the new one.[/b] We want this version 1.0 to be clear, fair, and fresh for everyone.[/*][/list]
[b]But starting over from zero doesn't mean starting with nothing.[/b]

We're thinking about [b]forms of recognition[/b] for players who have already invested time and energy in the game. It could take different forms, but always on condition that it recognizes your loyalty in a respectful way. We'll get back to this point in greater detail once the outlines of the overhaul are stable.

 

This is a difficult step, but it is necessary to give WAVEN a fighting chance. We had said that we would do everything we can to avoid this reset and, unfortunately, it will be a necessary measure for the good of the project.

 
[code]Please note:
[list]	[*][b]Cosmetic items bought with Gems or real currency will be kept[/b] or refunded if they can't be kept.[/*]	[*][b]Gems will be kept.[/b][/*]	[*][b]"Game comfort" elements bought with Gems[/b] (character slots, deck slots, etc.) [b]will be kept[/b] or refunded if necessary.[/*][/list][/code]
 
[h2][u]IN CONCLUSION[/u][/h2]
[b]WAVEN is changing.[/b]

We've taken the time to look reality in the face, examine our choices, and own up to our mistakes. What we are offering today is our determination to rebuilt on a solid foundation, with a clear direction and a game that deserves to exist in its own right, rather than for what we want it to be. There will obviously be adjustments, unexpected events, and probably a fumble or two. But this time, [b]we know where we are going[/b] and why we're going there. Thank you, all of you who are still with us. Thank you, all of you who are still here. And all of you who will come back. And all of you who, curious or skeptical, are still waiting to see before they believe. [b]We hope that this 2025 version will live up to your expectations and ours.[/b]

 

The WAVEN Team

notes.title: AnkamaLive: See You on April 4th
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/54a54f5819370ae1149ccccf292f0e3c8256751d.png[/img]

Behind every game is a story. Not just the story the game tells players, but also the story of what we experience while building the game… and [b]WAVEN's story is not a tranquil, flowing river.[/b]

 

We move ahead, we explore, we try things. Sometimes, we think we've got a great idea so we pursue it, it fits in with the rest… and then, too late, we realize that it causes a lot of problems. So we feel around, hesitate, test, wonder "Do we just own it and try to make it work?" but ultimately… no. We throw it all out. We try to understand what went wrong to avoid making the same mistake again. We get some perspective, we re-think our decisions, we start over. And all this for one and only one reason – [b]to make WAVEN a game worthy[/b] of a third era in the Krosmoz, a fantastic adventure.

 

Of course, this requires constant questioning, facing persistent doubts. Because even though we've made many strides since the beginning, we've also taken many steps backwards. [b]A project like WAVEN is a living thing that evolves, challenges your certainties and shakes up your very foundations.[/b] And when you start working on the foundations, everything else trembles. It shakes up the beliefs we though were solid, it challenges the decisions we've made with the very best of intentions… and it's frustrating. Frustrating because sometimes it feels like we're marching in place, losing time, spinning our wheels. The release of version 1.0? In 2023, we truly believed in it. Then reality caught up to us and we ran straight into a wall.

 

[b]So, where are we today?[/b]

 

We've made some important, sometimes radical, decisions, all with a single goal: [b]ensure that the game meets your expectations and ours.[/b] Our biggest focus right now? Progression – in the broad sense – and all the connections between it and the rest of the game. However, as is often the case with game design, changing one mechanic can have an impact on everything else. We need to share these repercussions with you along with our thinking, progress and vision.

 

[b]The WAVEN adventure is becoming clearer[/b] (finally!). We had promised a livestream at the start of the year. We're ready to talk. [b]It's time to make up for lost time and set things straight.[/b] And, to be blunt, [b]it's a lot.[/b]

 

[b]See you on Twitch* at 3 p.m. (CEST)/10 a.m. (EST) on April 4th, for a frank discussion with ToT about WAVEN's future.[/b]
[url=https://www.twitch.tv/ankamalive]twitch.tv/ankamalive[/url]
 

[i]* The livestream will take place in French, but subtitles in English, Spanish and Portuguese will be available directly in the platform.[/i]

notes.title: Special Season – Savara
notes.notes:
Hit fast, hit hard and… above all, don't stop. Iop has picked his chosen one – and, honestly, she packs a punch. Until [b]April 8,[/b] play as [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3021630/Savara/][b]Savara[/b][/url], determined to prove she's the greatest warrior in the World of Twelve! How? Easy! Wallop anything that moves. And if it doesn't move? Hit it again, just to be sure…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/6fa322442af6db4d4c84fee4acbdd486b4ef79f8.jpg[/img]

[b]"No one is born a champion – you become one!"[/b]

A thousand years (at least!) from now, her story will still be told… if she survives the training, of course. Because when Iop is watching, you don't ever want to disappoint! Savara, future champion, has been given a mission that requires [b]absolutely unprecedented strategic depth:[/b] [u]hit everything that moves.[/u]

 

She's always know she was destined for greatness – or at least that's what Iop whispered in her ear before getting distracted by something else and forgetting she even existed three seconds later. But no matter! A warrior worthy of the name forges their own destiny and, in passing, breaks a few jaws.

 

So, here is the ultimate form of training: leap head first into a horde of monsters and strike until the only thing that moves is a moofly. It might not be the tactical training she was dreaming of but… [b]Iop said "hit", so what's there to discuss?[/b]
[h2][u]Hit… hit again… hit some more, just in case![/u][/h2]
You'll be playing as [b]Savara,[/b] warming up before the major tournament of champions. Your goal? Grind everything in your path to dust. [b]Ten rounds, one rule:[/b] [u]hit hard.[/u]

 

Careful, though! Here, flailing around randomly with your fists is out of the question! You have [b]two sets of weapons:[/b] one [b]nice, strong cudgel[/b] for destructive heavy attacks, perfect for sending monsters flying into the bushes, and [b]two sharp daggers[/b] for a blur of ultra-fast combos, perfect for slicing your opponents into, well, thin (or thick) slices. Throw in [b]combo, heavy and ultimate attacks,[/b] rapid [b]sprints,[/b] and [b]dodges[/b] worthy of the Pig Ninja Clan and you get a perfectly chaotic brawl that's [u][b]jab[/b]solutely[/u] up Iop's alley.

 

And since the bearded god has decided to oversee all this himself, [b]he'll be giving her a few of his divine blessings…[/b] or at least throwing random items her way in hopes they'll help. A crown? A book? Doesn't matter, as long as you can hit with it! [b]After each wave is defeated,[/b] who knows what will drop!

 
[h2][u]An Absolute Arsenal Within Your Grasp![/u][/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/250d05a110f0ea89c15448df8c2b0821cac64be8.jpg[/img]

What's a legendary warrior without the appropriate style and accessories? With the [b]Platinum Pass,[/b] enjoy [b]fifty-six (56) items[/b] to perfect your champion look. Don the [b]Rhinobittybuto[/b] headgear, make an imposing [b]Champions' Entrance,[/b] or sprint with your faithful [b]Rhinobittybuto[/b] pet at your side… Iop might not have invented fashion, but he knows how to recognize a warrior with style! So, what are you waiting for? Head to the in-game Shop to show him you've got the class of a real champion!

[b]One parting tip – don't try to think too hard* about it or you might get hurt![/b]

[i]* Maybe don't think at all – that works too. You [/u]are[u] one of Iop's chosen ones, after all…[/i]

notes.title: WAKFU: Season 5 – Kickstarter
notes.notes:
[previewyoutube=iCG24gBg764;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]A fate thought to be sealed, a story that awakens…[/b]

After years of conflict, newly forged legends and shared emotions, the [b]The Brotherhood of the Tofu[/b] believed its [b]final chapter[/b] had been written, its story ending with the defeat of the Necros. We thought so too. But in the shadows, an [b]unexpected event[/b] came to pass.

 

A [b]mysterious character[/b] resurfaced, caught between two worlds, trapped in ice and engrossed with his thoughts: [b]Count Harebourg.[/b] It was thought he was had been lost during the fall of Oropo's Dimension, but he escaped the clutches of death. The Eliacube had decided otherwise. [b]Freed and exalted[/b] by [b]immense powers,[/b] his designs are far from peaceful…

[b]Long dormant under the ice, he is going to turn our heroes' adventure on its head.[/b]
[h2][u]Kickstarter Campaign[/u][/h2]
In 2020, thanks to YOU, we were able to [b]self-produce[/b] WAKFU Season 4. Almost [b]18,000 backers[/b] answered the call, raising [b]nearly 1.5 million euros.[/b] An [b]exceptional amount[/b] – a [b]European record[/b] – and, above all, [b]clear proof[/b] of your fondness for the Brotherhood of the Tofu!

 

[b]Today, we are no longer on our own.[/b]

Our partner, [i]France Télévisions[/i], told us they would like to join us on one last adventure with the Brotherhood, the very last, the "very, very last." Who could turn down one last adventure, on screen, for our beautiful band of heroes? We're promising you [b]twenty-six[/b] (26) [b]all-new episodes,[/b] twenty-six episodes showing the best of what we have to offer: our passion for art, storytelling and creativity. This last season is going to be a veritable [b]ode to WAKFU's legacy.[/b]

 

Thanks to our partners and regional support, a portion of the project is already financed. This will cover about 50-60% of the cost, and we are assuming the rest. It costs about €500,000 to produce one episode, so the total budget for the final season is 13 million euros.

[b]You support remains essential, so that is why we are launching a Kickstarter campaign.[/b]

By backing this project, [b]you will help us keep Ankama Animations independent[/b] and become [b]co-producers of WAKFU Season 5![/b] In addition, you'll receive some carefully crafted rewards for being such amazing fans – and, let's be honest too, we love to spoil you…

 

Depending on the tiers reached, we'll be taking things even further, with bonuses such as a [b]special episode,[/b] or even a [b]mini-series[/b] about the adventure and relationship of two characters whose story deserves to be explored and told…

[b]Time's a-ticking![/b]

Time's a ticking because our Kickstarter campaign can't run forever. [b]Our campaign starts today, Wednesday, February 12, and runs until Wednesday, March 12.[/b] One month to prove to the whole world – once again – [b]just how powerful the WAKFU community is![/b]

[b]Join us on the Kickstarter campaign page to learn more and participate:[/b]

[url=https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/ankamaanimations/wakfu-the-animated-series-season-5][b]BACK WAKFU![/b][/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33221747/0e1bd92db64cf2d78ee39523c346bab9d558077c.jpg[/img]

[h2][u]Follow the Campaign's Progress[/u][/h2]
Throughout this Kickstarter adventure, [b]we will be sharing every big moment with you,[/b] every goal we achieve, and every surprise we have in store for you. Whether on social media, our websites and forums and, naturally, on the [b]Kickstarter page for exclusive content,[/b] we'll be here to [b]keep you up to date,[/b] [b]answer your questions[/b] and [b]vibe with you.[/b] Together, we'll make this final season the stuff of legend!



[b]Just how far will this adventure through the eras of the Krosmoz take you?[/b]
[h3][b]The story continues with and, especially, thanks to you.[/b][/h3]

notes.title: Bad Seed Season: Get Out your Thorns and Push Back the Invaders.
notes.notes:
It is the year 1010 and Bwork Island has been deforested. Entirely? No! A small plot of resolute [b]weeds[/b] are doggedly resisting the invaders! [b]Until March 11,[/b] play as the resistance and push back the assaulting Bworks!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/ce7deb3cf629c99d3e3e6c3eb895cedcfa00899b.jpg[/img]

When it comes to colonizing land, the Bworks have one rule: [b]mow it all down and ransack everything.[/b] They assumed they could plant their banners and move into their cottages, but they overlooked one (tiny) detail… [b]the Weeds.[/b] And these ones can't be uprooted with a flick of the wrist. No, they can't. [b]They're tenacious, vengeful and ready to… fight.[/b]

 

Wha's worse is that the Bworks seem to have forgotten that [b]thorns and brambles are hiding under those petals.[/b] Honestly, they should have paid more attention to an obvious fact – if it grows on such arid and lifeless land, then it's built to survive! The hostilities have begun. They want to fight? They're gonna feel the thorns! No roots? No country!

 
[h2][u]Those Bworks Are Nuts…[/u][/h2]
 

[b]The battle will be fierce.[/b]

 

Play as the most beautiful representatives of the [b]Pest[/b] family – [b]Flowers[/b] – ready to fight to save their small plot of land from hordes of Bworks. Frenzied? Yes. Tireless? No. [b]They'll turn back after[/b] [b]10 turns.[/b]

 

Your [b]bouquet of resisters[/b] is lush: [b]Sunflowers[/b] turn the sun's energy into action points that let you plant more rebel flowers; the solidly-rooted [b]Belladarks[/b] form a wall of defense; the [b]Dandelions[/b] shoot their seeds and hit the first target in their crosshairs; and the [b]Dark Roses[/b] shoot seeds that pierce the entire line of Bworks and apply a penalty on their victims. And the [b]brambles?[/b] The Bworks better not step on them or they'll be disarmed… and covered in scratches by the time they get out!

 

Mother nature's child, you'll have a sizable advantage: the [b]sun.[/b] When efforts are at their peak, nearly insurmountable, shine one of its [b]Rays[/b] on one of your lovely plants and [b]it'll instantly recover some of its strength.[/b]

 

[b]Above all, protect your Sunflowers![/b] If one is trampled down, the game is over. And watch out… Bworks aren't the cleverest bunch but some call themselves [b]Cybworks.[/b] Believe us, you don't want to find out why…

 
[h2][u]A Garden of Rewards![/u][/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/f609c77bc95ceaf20f7d378dd0ac9b9c3a51d701.jpg[/img]

Everyone has the right to have their own secret garden… even Weeds. But never fear, we'll give you the garden tour! [b]A full fifty-six (56) flourishing rewards[/b] are waiting to be picked in the [b]Platinum Pass[/b] for this pastoral season, such as the [b]Millie-Rose[/b] pet, [b]Thick Brambles[/b] tracks and even the [b]Field Headgear.[/b] If you think you've got a green thumb, head over to the [b]in-game Shop now[/b] because everyone knows that even the most beautiful flowers wilt and the best deals never last forever.

 

[b]The Bworks want to garden, do they? They're going to reap trouble![/b]

notes.title: Happy New Year with WAVEN
notes.notes:
One year just came to an end and it's already time to hit the ground running for the next – no rest for the heroes, we want what comes next!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/b503a791b6d292c39a01ab6c72cee8c8fd6ff92c.jpg[/img]

Before anything else, [b]we wish you all the best for an excellent 2025.[/b] May this next chapter be signed success, happiness, friendship and health. [b]Thank you,[/b] also, for [b]being part of our dear community,[/b] sharing your [b]enthusiasm for WAVEN[/b] and coming along with us on this [b]incredible expedition[/b] across the seas of the World of Twelve.

 

The new year is always an opportunity to take a look back and contemplate how far you've come. Since the launch of early access, many wonderful, memorable things have happened:
[list]	[*]Nearly [b]sixty free updates[/b] with content and bugfixes.[/*]	[*]Approximately [b]twenty seasons[/b] that set the tempo for your adventure, each with its own unique challenge every month.[/*]	[*][b]Five new heroes[/b] – the Paladirs – joined the adventure.[/*]	[*][b]Three major expansions[/b] – the island nation of Amakna, Albuera and the Necroworld – with new islands to explore, feats to accomplish and treasures to collect.[/*]	[*][b]Krosmic Mode,[/b] offering a totally new gameplay experience.[/*]	[*]The [b]mobile release[/b] that made it possible for you to now continue your adventure wherever you are at all times.[/*]	[*]An [b]unforgettable[/b] [b]Ankama Convention[/b] to meet you, talk to you and rumble alongside you fighting the terrible Toross Mordal and his army.[/*]	[*]A [b]new book in Story Mode,[/b] continuing the investigations into the mysterious disappearance of the gods.[/*]	[*][b]Several hundred guilds[/b] [b]created,[/b] bringing together castaways to write their collective legends.[/*]	[*]All of this was possible thanks to a shared passion for creating and playing, the passion that brings the World of Twelve to life…[/*][/list]
 

The year 2024 was also marked by another [b]major event:[/b] [b]the much-awaited release of [u]WAKFU[/u] season four.[/b] This season transcended the screen to find its way into WAVEN with exclusive, related content paying homage to the series. Proof that the Krosmoz is still weaving its own story through our games and that [b]transmedia is still at the core of our vision,[/b] connecting worlds, stories, and players.

 
[h2][u]And Now?[/u][/h2]
The last time we came together to talk about the future was during the Ankama Convention. The discussions then both fueled hopes and raised questions or revealed frustrations for some of you, but know that our teams have never lost sight of the goal. We've focused our efforts on several areas:
[list]	[*][b]Rework progression,[/b] the spine that supports all gameplay loops and the very identity of WAVEN.[/*]	[*][b]Diversify game modes,[/b] with new content such as the boss fight and asynchronous mode (plus other surprises on the way).[/*]	[*][b]Correct and improve existing content,[/b] whether in regard to technical aspects or game design elements to make interactions smoother or deepen coherency in certain areas.[/*]	[*]And finally, [b]work on projects that are still under wraps[/b] but that we are eager to unveil when the time is right…[/*][/list]
 

[b]Our goal is still to make WAVEN a continuation and conclusion worthy of the Krosmoz trilogy.[/b] This is an important promise for us and we will do what we can to succeed. We are determined to achieve our ambitions in this regard. It is our commitment to you, and to the heritage that WAVEN represents.

 

This why we would like to get together with you in a livestream on Twitch in the [b]next few weeks[/b] to talk to you directly. Among our new year's resolutions for 2025, we want to [b]continue moving forward, hand in hand,[/b] fingers intertwined, with our community and in full [b]transparency.[/b] We have always shared our difficulties, for example the Unity update, and we cherish the relationship we have with you. We'll have some [b]great announcements[/b] to share! We'll schedule a date soon and hope you'll join us. For those who can't be there, a recap will be available on the official forum.

 

[b]In 2025, let's move forward together, united in our enthusiasm.
Thank you once again for being part of this incredible odyssey.[/b]

 

The WAVEN Team

notes.title: The Scalies are inviting you to discover the abysses this season
notes.notes:
Joe Searchall's been sniffing around again! Seeking vestiges of the world before, he's gone even deeper into the abyss. But this time, it isn't looking good for him because every search has its price and the locals intend to make that perfectly clear. Until [b]February 11,[/b] dive deep into the ocean depths and hold your breath – tightly because the ocean might never give it back…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/26e9d5bfb4316d54af72d4b85fb57be72496d642.jpg[/img]

For old Joe, anything that shines at the bottom of the ocean is an irresistible excuse to dive. Shipwrecks? Searched. Treasures? Brought to the surface. Sea monsters? "Landlubber nonsense!" If it shines, then it's worth its weight in kamas, and no fish will convince him otherwise! However… it appears that his [u]archaeo-lucrative[/u] digs have drawn the attention of some very bulging eyes – no, no, not Miranda's. Diving where even the Twelvian sun dares not penetrate, Joe has made a discovery… one that is very much alive. In the abyss lurks famished beasts – the Scalies. Going by the looks on their faces, they aren't pleased to have visitors. Tourists must not be welcome in these parts…

 

[b]Maybe they'll make an exception?[/b]

 
[h2][u]20,000 Fragments Under the Sea…[/u][/h2]
Under [b]Joe Searchall[/b]'s diving suit, you'll experience the scene as if you were there! Your mission? Don't get chewed up. [b]Survive five turns against waves of monsters[/b] that are as fishy as they are undesirably sticky.

 

Luckily, Joe wasn't born at low tide yesterday! Perhaps because of his extensive experience as a fearless diver, or simply because he's afraid of being eaten, the [u]sea[/u]soned diver is [b]remarkably good at gasping for air…[/b] [b]six[/b] times over. And that's a good thing, since that's [b]how many times he'll be able to attack[/b] these marine monsters that are dead-set on keeping him fathoms below the surface.

 

After each wave has been pushed back, mysterious artifacts will appear around you, providing that old sea dog Joe with [b]very useful powers.[/b] These powers can evolve, so make smart choices since no single one can ensure you make it to the surface in one piece! Don't waste any time choosing, either, because starting with the [b]seventh wave,[/b] [b]Snapsharks[/b] will set their fins on you – and they're no joke!

 

[b]All Joe wanted was to plunder the seas…[/b]
[h2][u]Treasures Ahoy![/u][/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/578fd7acd367bc0b204bb41e72d5f2a6e65c2f15.jpg[/img] 

For those who know the ropes when it comes to [b]good deals[/b] – unlike Joe – the season's [b]Platinum Pass[/b] is a real undersea treasure trove! A full [b]fifty-six (56) unique rewards[/b] could send old man Searchall into early retirement… It just goes to show that the ocean depths aren't entirely hostile and contain true marvels like the [b]Red Tunami pet,[/b] [b]the Scaly-Head headgear[/b] and the [b]Tenacious Seaweed halo.[/b] And if you want to unearth even more treasures worthy of an expert archaeologist, check out the [b]in-game Shop![/b]

 

[b]For Joe, everything that shines has a price; for the Scalies, everything that moves tastes good.[/b]

notes.title: It's a rat's life – rejection, corruption and sneaky tricks!
notes.notes:
It is Dr. Vik Taurenstein's sly pleasure to invite you to his modest laboratory, which was recently "relocated" to the [b]Time Portal[/b] for a "highly scientific and absolutely not insane" experiment, as he described it. His invitation is only good until [b]December 17[/b] so don't miss it!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/7a20a31aac3a0587fc44baf39d7ba87a3c946930.png[/img]

"I told you so!" he yelled to anyone who would – sadly for them – listen. Vik Taurenstein, the excentric scientist from the island nation of Brakmar, has been conducting rather dubious experiments ever since the Great Wave. Ignoring all the rules of ethics established by the Circle – the clan to which scientists in the World of Twelve belong – he was, unsurprisingly, kicked out of the community and shunned. For him, it seemed entirely logical that grafting two bow meows back-to-back would enable them to levitate. To his great dismay, you can imagine the results… And he's still yelling, "I told you I could do it!"

 

[b]Whatever has he come up with this time?![/b]

 

After dunking a rat in oil several times, and then in water – because: why not? – it was clear that the poor animal would never be the same. To everyone's surprise (especially the rat's), not only did the rodent's coat turn miraculously white, but its intelligence grew exponentially!

 
[h2][u]It's a rat's life – rejection, corruption and sneaky tricks![/u][/h2]

You'll play as this [b]Smart Rat,[/b] victim of an experiment conducted by your master of misfortune. Now that your intellectual abilities have become unmatched, you've been tossed aside, languishing in your [b]former cage,[/b] surrounded by [b]other rats.[/b] Rejected by them all because your coat is different from theirs.

[b]"Let's see if this one survives!"[/b]

You'll have to be clever to [b]turn them against each other![/b] Your torment will only last [b]10 turns[/b] – 10 turns to attempt to [b]convince the other rats[/b] to rally to your cause. What cause? It doesn't matter. You just need to survive, whatever it takes!

 

[b]Sway[/b] your former brother rodents in exchange for… food? [b]Recruit[/b] the rodents with foodstuffs represented by [b]points;[/b] the weaker they are, the easier they'll be to convince! Then, encourage them to kill each other – each recruited or dead rat [b]makes you stronger.[/b] Keep a sharp eye out, as [b]additional rats[/b] can swarm out of [b]holes[/b] spread about on the field.

 

As you go about your vile but delectable manipulations, you'll rack up new points; you can get them with [b]every blow[/b] you deal the rats, and when they [b]die.[/b] You don't have much room for maneuver, though, so you'll need to be cunning when dealing with the murine fellows who're after your hide – almost literally!

 

Between two rounds of negotiations (or bites), you'll spot a rat tha's not like the others – the [b]Merchant Rat[/b]. Greedy, especially when it comes to food, he wants to take advantage of the dissent to do business with you… Use your hard-won crumbs to buy "[b]treasures[/b]" from him that will give you [b]temporary or permanent bonuses[/b] depending on their rarity. Be careful not to offend him, though… Who knows what he could do if he feels threatened?

 
[h2][u]G[u]rat[/u]ifying Souvenirs![/u][/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/384fcf496196d6790156afb3578e063d2ccc03d6.jpg[/img]

They say that life is a series of opportunities, but yours has been full of obstacles! As compensation for Dr. Vik Taurenstein's failed and "ratty" experiment, you could treat yourself to a few delights by getting a [b]Platinum Pass.[/b] What do you think? There are a full [b]56 souvenirs[/b] of your rat's life to take with you, such as a [b]Ratilton pet,[/b] [b]Pointy Ears[/b] headgear, or even [b]Wily Piper[/b] tracks, and more. If you swing by the [b]in-game Shop[/b] now, you might be able to turn things around – instead of rats being bad omens, you* can be the bad omen!

 

[i]* Well, you'll be disguised as a rat, that is. Does that count?[/i]

notes.title: Ankama Show Time: Join Us on December 18!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44049144/fc1a0b3d382aa60e5760ddd58eec7dd78ed33df1.jpg[/img]

[b][i]Adiós,[/i] [i]KrosmoNote[/i]…[/b]

 

KrosmoNote, after five wonderful years, it's time for us to part ways. We've shared some incredible moments together… Remember the very first time we celebrated 15 years of DOFUS? And now the game has just celebrated its 20th birthday. And do you remember when the world went into lockdown? Faithful to your post, you warmed our hearts, much more than this fake hearth.

 

We shared some difficult times and the best laughs as well. But it's time to move on. No, KrosmoNote, don't make this more difficult than it needs to be. Leave… And don't come back. No, it's not you, it's just that… We've found someone else, someone better!

 

[b]Meet [i]Ankama Show Time![/i][/b]

 

[b][i]Ankama Show Time[/i][/b] is [b][i]an unmissable[/i][/b] event for all adventurers of the Krosmoz and of the world of Ankama in general. [b][i]Ankama Show Time[/i][/b] is [b]YOUR[/b] date (lucky devils!) with our teams to talk about the future, our upcoming projects, your next adventures, and to give you some amazing sneak peeks, previews and exclusive information. [b][i]Ankama Show Time[/i][/b] is therefore the [b]ultimate stream[/b] to watch [b]live[/b] or [b]on demand[/b] to [b]ensure you don't miss any[/b] Ankama news.

 

[b]Games, Animations, Publications: the whole family together![/b]

 

At the heart of this large family: [b]transmedia[/b] – our band leader since the beginning, the one that makes us march to the beat of the same drum and makes our inspirations, voices and passions sing in harmony. [b][i]Ankama Show Time,[/i][/b] as you've probably guessed, is our chance to unveil the [b]theme that will drive all our projects[/b] for the coming year.

 
[h2][u]It's showtime![/u][/h2]
Wait! How about we build up some hype and give you some deets on what to expect?

 
[h3]Before[/h3]
While streaming live, our content creation partners will speculate, theorize and discuss topics with you, alongside a few Ankamians… who will do their best not to crack faced with all your questions!

 
[h3]The show[/h3]
The main event: A [b]prerecorded session about 30 minutes long,[/b] during which we'll unveil (finally!) the year's theme, how it will be woven into our various projects and games, especially regarding DOFUS, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/215080/WAKFU/][b]WAKFU[/b][/url], DOFUS Touch, DOFUS Retro and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3021630/Savara/][b]Savara[/b][/url]. This will also be an opportunity to make [b]a big announcement[/b] regarding a certain and much-loved animated series…

 
[h3]After[/h3]
Back to the livestream: Hosted by the same content creators and Ankamians, they will chat with you and recap everything that was revealed while providing more details for some topics.

 

[b]So… All aboard the hype train?[/b]

 

[h2][u]What about WAVEN?[/u][/h2]
As you know, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2343650/Waven/][b]WAVEN[/b][/url] is in early access at the moment, and some major changes are currently being planned. They decided to decline our invitation so that they could talk to you at the start of the year in a special livestream. So, some big announcements are in store for the Castaways!

 

[b]SAVE THE DATE![/b]

[b]Ankama Show Time – December 18 at 6:30 p.m. CET[/b]

[b]LIVE*[/b] on…

[url=https://www.twitch.tv/AnkamaLive]twitch.tv/ankamalive[/url]

Watch the [i][b]REPLAY**[/b][/i] on…

[url=https://www.youtube.com/@ankama]youtube.com/@ankama[/url]

 

[i]* This stream will be hosted in French, but subtitles automatically generated by the Twitch platform will be available.[/i]

 

[i]** The replay on YouTube will include subtitles translated by our teams in English, Spanish and Portuguese.[/i]
